thread.title: Qualcomm drops NXP acquisition, leaves analysts concerned about Apple business

author: morningstar.com
title: Qualcomm drops NXP acquisition, leaves analysts concerned about Apple business
text:
By Emily Bary
Several price-target hikes follow better-than-expected earnings
Nearly two years after Qualcomm Inc. announced its intent to acquire NXP Semiconductors NV, investors are pleased that the company is moving on.
Qualcomm (QCOM) announced in conjunction with its earnings report Wednesday that it was walking away from the NXPI deal, which failed to get Chinese regulatory approval by the companies' deadline. Qualcomm also reported better-than-expected earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/qualcomm-plan-to-kill-nxp-deal-earnings-beat-send-stock-popping-higher-2018-07-25).
Shares are up 3.2% after Qualcomm's various announcements, and at least 10 analysts raised their price targets on the stock, per a FactSet count. Yet questions remain about the company's trajectory going forward.
Don't miss: This FAANG stock looks like the next Berkshire Hathaway -- a smart bet for the next 25 years (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-faang-stock-looks-like-the-next-berkshire-hathway-a-smart-bet-for-25-years-2018-07-26)
"On the positive, closure on NXPI, even with the disappointing (to the company) no-deal outcome will likely be welcome for investors, as will the $30 billion buyback," Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon wrote. "Additionally, we do not want to minimize the potential for possibly settling the Huawei disagreement (which has been ongoing for over a year), which could bring back $1 billion-plus in licensing revenues back into the fold."
That said, he also wrote that Qualcomm's core business "is still getting somewhat worse versus expectations." In addition, the company was vague on timing for the buyback, which struck Rasgon and some other analysts as a walk-back of prior commentary.
Rasgon rates the stock at market perform with a $65 target.
Opinion:Qualcomm claims wireless dominance over Intel and Apple (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/qualcomm-claims-wireless-dominance-over-intel-and-apple-2018-07-23)
Canaccord Genuity analyst T. Michael Walkley raised his price target to $81 from $75 after the report, writing that the company looks well-positioned on a number of fronts. "Due to strong Snapdragon 700 and 800 sales to Chinese OEMs, QCT posted stronger sales and margins than our estimates," he wrote, referring to the company's CDMA technologies business.
"With Qualcomm indicating its guidance assumes its thin modems are not included in Apple's upcoming new iPhones, the [mobile-station modem] guidance of 205 million to 225 million was well ahead of our 177 million estimate," he said.
In addition, Walkley is upbeat about the company's status in 5G and wrote that Qualcomm appears to be a year or two ahead of peers when it comes to development.
Not all were optimistic, however. Morgan Stanley's James Faucette reiterated his underweight rating, writing that the NXP news could actually be a negative.
"We viewed NXPI as a uniquely strategic asset and see limited alternatives that would similarly accelerate Qualcomm's expansion into market adjacencies and offer incremental operating leverage," he wrote.
See also: Broadcom deal to buy CA makes little sense on the surface (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/broadcom-deal-to-buy-ca-makes-little-sense-on-the-surface-2018-07-11)
Meanwhile Qualcomm's "positioning with Apple" (AAPL) is getting worse, he said, judging from the announcement about basebands (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/qualcomm-suggests-apple-will-use-intel-modems-in-new-iphone-2018-07-25) in the new iPhones.
"Qualcomm had historically maintained share for iPhone SKUs serving CDMA-based carriers, but with Apple now intent on displacing Qualcomm entirely, Qualcomm does not have its typical negotiating leverage as an important chipset supplier," he wrote. The implication is that Apple will solely rely on Intel Corp. (INTC) with the new phones.
Faucette maintained his $55 price target.
Shares are up 17% over the past 12 months, while the S&P 500 has gained 15%.
-Emily Bary; 1231ET
